data.name: All Fall Down
data.detailed_description:
Set in a distant futuristic world, this is a unique first person shooter/platform game, with a puzzle or two included.

You find yourself woken up from a snooze by load thudding noises, you look out your apartment window, why is all the debris falling?
Here starts your adventure to save your world from destruction, locate and flick Switches (using your bullets) to proceed up the emergency pillars, clear levels , complete mazes, jump over vertigo inducing bridge blocks with your jet pack if needed, to eventually find out what is going on and stop the debris from falling to save your planet!

Shoot the falling debris with your bullets, to defend yourself.
Build Blocks or use the fallen debris and build bridges, obstacles that can help you complete levels.

reviews.review:
All Fall Down is a compact science-fiction adventure that tries to accomplish more than its straightforward first-person presentation initially suggests. Developed and published by khos85, the game combines shooting, exploration, platforming, and puzzle solving within a futuristic world facing an extraordinary catastrophe. Debris is falling from above in enormous quantities, placing the world in danger and leaving the player responsible for discovering what is causing the phenomenon. This mystery gives the journey a clear purpose while providing a narrative explanation for the hazardous environments the player must navigate.

Rather than concentrating entirely on gunplay, All Fall Down regularly shifts attention between different types of challenges. Combat is part of the experience, but players are also expected to traverse difficult areas, investigate their surroundings, and solve environmental problems. This variety makes the game feel closer to an experimental first-person adventure than a conventional shooter. Its structure can be appealing to players who enjoy having exploration and problem solving between action sequences, although anyone expecting constant combat may find its pacing considerably different from a traditional FPS.

The platforming mechanics play an important role in making movement itself part of the challenge. Navigating from a first-person perspective can produce a stronger feeling of actually occupying the environment, particularly when crossing dangerous spaces or attempting carefully positioned jumps. However, first-person platforming naturally introduces some difficulty in judging distances and landing positions. This can occasionally make traversal feel less precise than it would from a third-person viewpoint, but it also contributes to the game's emphasis on environmental navigation rather than treating movement merely as transportation between battles.

Puzzle solving further distinguishes the experience. Progress is not always determined by eliminating enemies, and players need to examine locations and understand how particular obstacles can be overcome. These moments encourage slower and more deliberate exploration. The puzzles, platforming sections, and combat encounters work together to prevent the gameplay from settling permanently into one rhythm. While none of these individual systems possesses exceptional depth, their combination gives the game a recognizable personality and demonstrates the developer's willingness to experiment with several gameplay ideas inside one project.

The science-fiction setting is arguably more memorable for its premise than for its visual sophistication. A world being overwhelmed by mysterious falling debris is a strange and effective foundation for an adventure because the disaster is directly connected to the player's objective. Instead of simply being told that civilization is threatened, the player moves through environments shaped by that crisis while searching for answers. The central question of where the debris originates and how the catastrophe can be stopped supplies enough mystery to maintain forward momentum without requiring an excessively complicated narrative.

Presentation is one area where expectations should remain realistic. All Fall Down is an independent production from 2015, and its graphics, environmental detail, animation, and overall technical finish reflect its limited scale and age. It cannot match the visual polish or mechanical refinement of larger first-person releases. Some aspects can consequently feel dated or rough, particularly when compared directly with modern games. Nevertheless, the project has an unmistakably experimental quality that gives it a certain charm. Its appeal comes from seeing how its different concepts fit together rather than from spectacular production values.

The mixture of genres is simultaneously one of the game's greatest strengths and one of its limitations. Combining shooting, puzzles, exploration, and first-person platforming gives the player more activities to engage with, but it also means the experience lacks the specialization of games devoted entirely to one mechanic. The shooting is not sophisticated enough to carry the game by itself, while the puzzles and platforming are better viewed as complementary elements rather than exceptionally elaborate standalone systems. Players willing to accept this balance are more likely to appreciate what the developer attempted.

All Fall Down is therefore most suitable for players interested in unusual and relatively obscure independent projects. There is something appealing about a game willing to construct an entire adventure around the bizarre idea of catastrophic debris raining onto a futuristic world. The experience has imperfections, but it does not simply imitate the structure of a standard shooter. Exploration matters, movement can become a challenge, puzzles provide changes of pace, and combat adds danger when needed. Together, these ingredients create a modest but distinctive journey.

Ultimately, All Fall Down is more successful as an ambitious indie experiment than as a highly polished first-person adventure. Its technical limitations and occasionally rough execution are noticeable, yet its genre blending and unusual premise prevent it from feeling completely ordinary. The mysterious catastrophe provides an effective reason to explore, while the combination of shooting, platforming, and puzzles offers enough variety to sustain interest for players receptive to older independent games. Developed and published by khos85, it is an imperfect but imaginative project whose ideas are often more impressive than its execution. 

Rating: 6/10
